extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to the journal Mathematics of Computation (computational mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting research articles to the AMS journal Mathematics of Computation, including scope, submission format, peer-review model, and post-acceptance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article suitability / Aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must be of significant computational interest and contain original and substantial mathematical analysis or development of computational methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas covered include numerical analysis, computational discrete mathematics (including number theory, algebra and combinatorics), and related fields such as stochastic numerical methods. Submissions should address topics of significant computational interest and present original, substantial contributions rather than minor incremental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics of Computation has a single-anonymous peer-review process in which the reviewers know who the authors of the manuscript are, but the authors do not have access to the information on who the peer reviewers are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All articles appearing in the journal are peer reviewed by external reviewers. Be prepared for external evaluation of scientific content and presentation. For initial submission questions contact the journal's provided email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' right to desk-reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission ensure your paper fits the journal's scope and is strong in content and presentation; poor presentation or out-of-scope subject matter can lead to immediate rejection without external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission frequency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are limited to three submissions within any 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit applies to submissions to Mathematics of Computation; plan and prioritize submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method and required metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sending a paper copy, include: name of the journal, name of the corresponding author, contact information including email and mailing address, and suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper. Ensure all contact information, particularly email addresses, is supplied to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / No simultaneous or prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript is original and not under review or published elsewhere before submitting; violation may result in rejection or other sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required. It must be brief, reasonably self-contained, and not exceed 300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an abstract that summarizes the main results and methods concisely; the AMS offers free worldwide access to electronic abstracts so craft the abstract to be informative to a broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify appropriate primary and secondary MSC codes (2020 revision) and include them in the paper's footnotes to help editors and reviewers place the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance author obligations (consent and copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement. If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online Submission Instructions after acceptance. Be prepared to complete consent and copyright paperwork and, for OA articles, select an appropriate CC license. Coordinate authorship agreements before acceptance to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AMS style files and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX resources, the AMS Style Guide, and journal article templates (including Overleaf templates). Using these resources helps ensure compliance with AMS formatting and can reduce delays during production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and preparation of graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and tools are provided for preparing accessible mathematics content and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the 'Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content' and AMS resources on preparing graphics to make content accessible and compliant with AMS production standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and inquiries about accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inquiries concerning a paper that has been accepted for publication that cannot be answered via the manuscript tracking system should be sent to the Electronic PrePress Department (email or postal address provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance, use the manuscript tracking system first; if questions remain, contact the Electronic PrePress Department at the AMS with the provided postal and email contact details.
